title: Clearance Sacrifice
subtitle: Give up a piece to vacate the one square that matters.
goals: Spot when your own piece is in the way
Vacate lines and squares with tempo

steps.say: Sometimes the piece blocking your winning idea is YOUR OWN. A clearance sacrifice throws that piece away — ideally with check or a threat — so the piece behind it can strike. You're not sacrificing FOR material; you're paying rent on a square. Look at this position: your queen and bishop form a battery on the b1–h7 diagonal... except your own knight stands on e4, right in the way.

steps.prompt: Your knight blocks your own queen-bishop battery. Clear the diagonal — with check — and mate!
hints: The knight must move ANYWHERE to open the diagonal — but the best clearance moves come with check, so Black never gets a breath.
Nf6+!! — whether Black captures or ducks, the diagonal is open and Qxh7 is mate.

line.say: Clearance with check! The knight steps off the diagonal AND forces the reply — Black can capture or duck, but cannot fix h7...
The battery fires: queen takes h7, bishop guards her from b1. The knight didn't die for material — it died for one empty square on a diagonal. That's clearance.

rejections.say: The diagonal is open... but with no check, Black gets one move — ...g6! — and the mate is gone forever. Clearance must come WITH TEMPO: Nf6+!
It clears the diagonal and eyes h7 — but no check! Black plays ...h6 or ...g6 and survives. The clearance square is f6: check first, mate second.

steps.wrongSay: Any knight move opens the diagonal — but only ONE does it with check. Find it.
steps.successSay: When your attack looks blocked, check whether the roadblock is your own piece — then sell it with tempo.

steps.prompt: Same position, deeper question: Black could DECLINE the knight with ...Kh8 instead of capturing. Prove the sacrifice still mates — play it against the decline.
hints: If the king ducks to h8, is h7 any better defended? Count again.
Nf6+ Kh8, and Qxh7 is STILL mate — now the knight even guards the queen a second time.

line.say: Mate anyway — declined sacrifices must be checked too, and this one is airtight: the queen is guarded by the b1 bishop AND now by the f6 knight. A true clearance sac works against every reply.

rejections.say: The diagonal opens — but without check, and Black plays ...g6 with time to spare. Only the f6 check denies Black that single saving tempo. (And notice: before ANY knight move, Qh7 wasn't even legal — your own knight blocked the queen's path. That's the whole lesson.)

steps.wrongSay: Same first move as before — the point is what happens when Black doesn't take.
steps.successSay: Capture or decline, the diagonal opens and h7 falls. Verified against every defense — like all your sacrifices should be.
